s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction with highly vascularized mass
salient_findings: Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Considerable uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy regarding rib and vertebral lesions
key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Sinonasal tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy
Serum thyroglobulin was significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results confirmed VTC metastasis in both costal and sinonasal tumor biopsies

shortlist.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum thyroglobulin and biopsy results confirmed VTC metastasis

shortlist.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypervascular tumor with distant metastases and elevated serum thyroglobulin

shortlist.label: Tall cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive behavior and metastatic potential consistent with clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Columnar cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but aggressive subtype with potential for distant metastases

shortlist.label: Hürthle cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible consideration given thyroid origin and metastatic disease

raw.rationale: The combination of highly vascularized masses in the nasal cavities, elevated serum thyroglobulin, and biopsy-confirmed VTC metastasis in both costal and sinonasal tumors, along with the presence of metastases in the rib and vertebra as shown by CT scan and radioiodine scintigraphy, strongly supports VTC metastasis as the diagnosis.

rejected.label: Papillary Thyroid Cancer
rejected.why: While papillary thyroid cancer can metastasize, the specific findings of vertebral and rib metastases, along with the biopsy results and imaging studies, more strongly support VTC metastasis.
